sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I'm going to tell you a story first about how a building got designed.
sentences.zh: 首先，我要给你们讲一个关于某座建筑如何设计的故事。

sentences.en: A very unusual building in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约一座非常不同寻常的建筑。

sentences.en: The Citicorp Tower.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团中心大楼。

sentences.en: When it was built in 1977, Citicorp Center was, at 59 stories, the 7th tallest building in the world.
sentences.zh: 1977年建成时，59层的花旗集团中心是当时世界上第七高的建筑。

sentences.en: You know, I can still remember the first time I saw the Citicorp Center.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我至今还记得第一次见到花旗集团中心时的情景。

sentences.en: As you exit the local 6th subway station at Lexington and 53rd in Midtown Manhattan, you're confronted by a sheer 915-foot building face shooting up right from your feet.
sentences.zh: 当你从曼哈顿中城列克星敦大道和53街的地铁站出来时，一座915英尺高的建筑立面会直接从你脚下拔地而起，扑面而来。

sentences.en: That's reporter Joel Werner.
sentences.zh: 那是记者乔尔·沃纳。

sentences.en: With its gleaming facade of glass and steel and striking 45-degree angle crown,
sentences.zh: 凭借其闪闪发光的玻璃钢结构外立面和引人注目的45度角顶部，

sentences.en: the Citicorp Center is truly one of the most spectacular skyscrapers on a skyline known for its spectacular skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团中心确实是这座以壮观摩天大楼闻名的天际线上，最壮观的摩天大楼之一。

sentences.en: But really, it's the base of the building that takes your breath away.
sentences.zh: 但真正让人叹为观止的，其实是这座建筑的底部。

sentences.en: This massive 59-storey skyscraper levitates mid-air, hovering 115 feet above the street corner.
sentences.zh: 这座巨大的59层摩天大楼悬浮在半空中，悬停在街道拐角上方115英尺处。

sentences.en: At first glance, the building seems to violate the basic laws of physics.
sentences.zh: 乍一看，这座建筑似乎违反了基本的物理定律。

sentences.en: When you look up, you look directly at the underside of the building corner.
sentences.zh: 当你抬头看时，你会直接看到建筑拐角的底部。

sentences.en: It overhangs the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 它悬挑在人行道上方。

sentences.en: I mean, we'd expect a column or even the grounds.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们本以为会有柱子，甚至会有地基。

sentences.en: Instead, there's nothing.
sentences.zh: 然而，那里什么都没有。

sentences.en: Just thin air.
sentences.zh: 只有稀薄的空气。

sentences.en: Of course, the building isn't really levitating.
sentences.zh: 当然，这座建筑并不是真的在悬浮。

sentences.en: It's propped up on stilts, which join the building at the midpoint of each side.
sentences.zh: 它由高跷般的支柱支撑，这些支柱在每一侧的中点与建筑相连。

sentences.en: It does not look sturdy.

sentences.en: But it's got to be sturdy.
sentences.zh: 但它必须稳固。

sentences.en: It's got to be safe, or they wouldn't have built it this way.
sentences.zh: 它必须安全，否则他们就不会这样建造它。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's the secret about this building.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是关于这座建筑的秘密。

sentences.en: And it was literally a secret for nearly two decades after it was built.
sentences.zh: 而且在它建成后的近二十年里，这确实是一个秘密。

sentences.en: The Citicorp Center could very well have blown over in the wind.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团中心很有可能在风中被吹倒。

sentences.en: What I wanted to know was when was this building going to fall down?
sentences.zh: 我想知道的是，这座建筑什么时候会倒塌？

sentences.zh: 我想，这东西真的有大麻烦了。

sentences.en: This brand new skyscraper was on the verge of catastrophic failure.
sentences.zh: 这栋全新的摩天大楼正处于灾难性倒塌的边缘。

sentences.en: But the imminent disaster wasn't the result of one glaring oversight.
sentences.zh: 但迫在眉睫的灾难并非源于某一个明显的疏忽。

sentences.en: Rather, it was a sequence of minor issues.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是一系列小问题叠加的结果。

sentences.en: Let's remember how we got here.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: This building was on stilts because they had to build over the church.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑之所以架在支柱上，是因为它必须建在教堂上方。

sentences.en: And stilts placed at the corners would have been just fine.
sentences.zh: 如果支柱放在四个角上，本来是完全没问题的。

sentences.en: Except the church was at the corner of the lot.
sentences.zh: 但问题是教堂正好位于地块的角落。

sentences.en: So the stilts had to be in the middle of each face.
sentences.zh: 所以支柱不得不放在每条边的中间。

sentences.en: And that could have been A-OK.
sentences.zh: 这本来也完全可以。

sentences.en: Except the offset stilts led LeMessier to use an ultralight chevron bracing structure.
sentences.zh: 但偏置的支柱导致勒梅西耶（LeMessier）使用了超轻的人字形支撑结构。

sentences.en: Which would have been perfectly adequate.
sentences.zh: 这种结构本来也完全够用。

sentences.en: Except in the end, those chevron Vs were bolted, not welded together.
sentences.zh: 但最终，那些人字形的“V”字结构是用螺栓连接的，而不是焊接在一起的。

sentences.en: And even that could have been fine.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，本来也可能没问题。

sentences.en: Except no one thought about how vulnerable this crazy design was to wind blowing at its corners.
sentences.zh: 但没人想到这个疯狂的设计在面对吹向角落的风时是多么脆弱。

sentences.en: No one except an anonymous college student.
sentences.zh: 除了一个匿名的大学生，没人想到。

sentences.en: LeMessier went to Citicorp chairman Walter Wriston and told him they would need to open up the building and weld it back together.
sentences.zh: 勒梅西耶找到花旗集团董事长沃尔特·里斯顿（Walter Wriston），告诉他必须打开建筑并重新焊接加固。

sentences.en: And he said, how much is it going to cost?
sentences.zh: 他问：“这要花多少钱？”

sentences.en: I don't think it's going to cost an awful lot.
sentences.zh: “我想不会花太多钱。”

sentences.en: A million or two?
sentences.zh: “一两百万？”

sentences.en: That's nothing for a building that costs 175 minutes and if it falls down.
sentences.zh: “对于一座造价1.75亿美元且面临倒塌风险的建筑来说，这根本不算什么。”

sentences.en: From here, LeMessier and his team worked with the Citicorp bigwigs to coordinate emergency repairs on the building.
sentences.zh: 此后，勒梅西耶和他的团队与花旗集团的高层合作，协调对大楼进行紧急维修。

sentences.en: With the help of the NYPD, they worked out an evacuation plan spanning a 10-block radius.
sentences.zh: 在纽约警局的帮助下，他们制定了一项覆盖方圆10个街区的疏散计划。

sentences.en: They had 2,500 Red Cross volunteers on standby and three different weather services employed 24-7 to keep an eye on potential windstorMs.
sentences.zh: 他们安排了2500名红十字会志愿者待命，并雇用了三家不同的气象服务机构全天候监测潜在的风暴。

sentences.en: They welded through the night and quit at daybreak, just as the building occupants returned to work.
sentences.zh: 他们彻夜焊接，在天亮时停工，正好赶在大楼里的住户回来上班前。

sentences.en: But all this happened in secret, over three months, without telling anyone who worked there.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是秘密进行的，持续了三个月，没有告诉任何在那里工作的人。

sentences.en: Which is the part of the story I kind of have a problem with.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个故事中我有点难以接受的部分。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't this situation serious enough to warrant informing the building's tenants?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种情况难道不严重到足以告知大楼的租户吗？

sentences.en: My wife works in a skyscraper in midtown Manhattan and you know, it's about informed consent.
sentences.zh: 我妻子在曼哈顿中城的一座摩天大楼里工作，你知道，这关乎知情同意权。

sentences.en: I'd want her to be able to make the judgement call about whether or not to go work in a faulty building.
sentences.zh: 我希望她能自己做出判断，决定是否要在一座有缺陷的建筑里工作。

sentences.en: Not to have it made for her.
sentences.zh: 而不是由别人替她做决定。

sentences.en: Their thinking was, a contingency plan was in place and ready to be invoked as soon as a storm strong enough to blow the building down was in striking distance of New York.
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是，应急预案已经就绪，一旦有足以吹倒大楼的风暴进入纽约的打击范围，就会立即启动。

sentences.en: Except...
sentences.zh: 然而……

sentences.en: There was a giant storm racing up the east coaSt.
sentences.zh: 当时有一场巨大的风暴正沿着东海岸北上。

sentences.en: Hurricane Ella.
sentences.zh: 飓风“艾拉”（Ella）。

sentences.en: LeMessier says the powers that be were just hours away from calling in the evacuation.
sentences.zh: 勒梅西耶说，当时掌权者距离下令疏散仅有几个小时之遥。

sentences.en: But the hurricane veered into the Atlantic before it hit New York, and in the end, the public was never notified.
sentences.zh: 但飓风在袭击纽约前转向进入了大西洋，最终，公众从未被告知此事。

sentences.en: And I know what you're thinking.
sentences.zh: 我知道你在想什么。

sentences.en: If only there was some kind of independent organisation that serves the public's right to know,
sentences.zh: 要是当时有某种独立的组织来维护公众的知情权就好了，

sentences.en: that might wonder why Citicorp Centre was aglow with blowtorches all night every night.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会好奇为什么花旗集团中心每晚都灯火通明，焊枪火花四溅。

sentences.en: You know, something like a newspaper.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像报纸那样的机构。

sentences.en: Except...
sentences.zh: 然而……

sentences.en: The New York Times was on strike.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》当时正在罢工。

sentences.en: Not only did the New York Times go on strike, but all the newspapers in New York went on strike until October.
sentences.zh: 不仅是《纽约时报》，纽约所有的报纸都罢工到了十月份。

sentences.en: So we had a press blackout, and that was the greatest thing that ever happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我们遭遇了新闻封锁，而那竟是发生过的最棒的事情。

sentences.en: So word never got out, and construction was finished.
sentences.zh: 因此消息从未传出，施工也完成了。

sentences.en: And Citicorp Centre has remained standing ever since, long enough to be renamed Citigroup Centre and later 601 Lexington.
sentences.zh: 花旗集团中心自此一直屹立不倒，直到后来更名为花旗集团中心，再后来又改名为列克星敦大道601号。

sentences.en: And this whole thing remained a secret for almost 20 years.
sentences.zh: 而整件事作为秘密隐藏了近20年。

sentences.en: In the early 90s, writer Joe Morgenstern overheard the story being told at a party.
sentences.zh: 90年代初，作家乔·摩根斯特恩（Joe Morgenstern）在一次聚会上无意中听到了这个故事。

sentences.en: He interviewed LeMessier and broke the story in The New Yorker in 1995.
sentences.zh: 他采访了勒梅西耶，并在1995年的《纽约客》上披露了这个故事。

sentences.en: LeMessier went on to tell the story publicly, like he did at MIT, which is how we have him talking about this.
sentences.zh: 勒梅西耶后来公开讲述了这个故事，就像他在麻省理工学院所做的那样，这就是我们现在能听到他谈论此事的由来。

sentences.en: And, after the story got out, it was written up as a textbook case of good ethics in structural engineering.
sentences.zh: 而且，在故事传开后，它被写成了结构工程中职业道德的教科书级案例。

sentences.en: New York was spared a tremendous loss of life and the annihilation of its skyline,
sentences.zh: 纽约避免了一场巨大的生命损失和天际线的毁灭，

sentences.en: all because Bill LeMessier was humble enough to give time to the inquiry of an undergraduate student.
sentences.zh: 这一切都归功于比尔·勒梅西耶足够谦逊，愿意花时间去回应一名本科生的询问。

sentences.en: Thank goodness for this uppity college senior and his thesis,
sentences.zh: 感谢这位“傲慢”的大学高年级学生和他的论文，

sentences.en: and kudos to Bill LeMessier, who, through his humility and heroism, saves the day.
sentences.zh: 也要向比尔·勒梅西耶致敬，他凭借谦逊和英雄主义，拯救了一切。

sentences.en: And, uh, that's really the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，故事到这里就真的结束了。

sentences.en: Except...
sentences.zh: 然而……

sentences.en: Now, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: There are a couple of more things here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有几件事。

sentences.en: Let's take a step back and remember how this story starts.
sentences.zh: 让我们退后一步，回顾一下这个故事是如何开始的。

sentences.en: I got a call from a student.
sentences.zh: 我接到了一个学生的电话。

sentences.en: He was a real student from New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 他是一个来自新泽西州的真实学生。

sentences.en: He was an architectural student.
sentences.zh: 他是一名建筑系学生。

sentences.en: And this teacher had given him this building to study.
sentences.zh: 老师给了他这座建筑作为研究课题。

sentences.en: I do not know the school.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是哪所学校。

sentences.en: I wish he would call me.
sentences.zh: 我希望他能给我打个电话。

sentences.en: The way LeMessier tells it, and how Joe Morgenstern told it in The New Yorker,
sentences.zh: 按照勒梅西耶的讲述，以及乔·摩根斯特恩在《纽约客》中的描述，

sentences.en: the college student, the young hero of our story, was lost to history.
sentences.zh: 那个大学生，我们故事里的年轻英雄，在历史上被遗忘了。

sentences.en: Okay, wait for it.
sentences.zh: 好了，等着看。

sentences.en: Wait for this moment.
sentences.zh: 等待这一刻。

sentences.en: It's a good one.
sentences.zh: 这可是个好戏。

sentences.en: Here it comes.
sentences.zh: 它来了。

sentences.en: It would have been sometime in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 那应该是在90年代初的某个时候。

sentences.en: I remember being upstairs in my bedroom and had one of my sons.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时在楼上的卧室里，带着我的一个儿子。

sentences.en: He was sort of hanging off me as I was trying to put him down to go to bed.
sentences.zh: 当我正试图把他放下睡觉时，他正挂在我身上。

sentences.en: And, um, suddenly my husband, who had been downstairs,
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯，突然我丈夫，他当时在楼下，

sentences.en: started yelling a little bit and saying,
sentences.zh: 开始大声喊叫，说道：

sentences.en: Diane!
sentences.zh: “黛安！”

sentences.en: Diane!
sentences.zh: “黛安！”

sentences.en: Quick, quick, turn on the TV.
sentences.zh: “快，快，打开电视。”

sentences.en: Your thesis building is on TV.
sentences.zh: “你的论文建筑在电视上。”

sentences.en: This is Diane Hartley.
sentences.zh: 这是黛安·哈特利（Diane Hartley）。

sentences.en: As far as we can tell, she was the student in LeMessier's story.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，她就是勒梅西耶故事里的那个学生。

sentences.en: And so I, you know, holding the baby with one arm,
sentences.zh: 于是我，你知道，一只手抱着孩子，

sentences.en: I fumbled for the remote and got to the channel just in time to hear.
sentences.zh: 我摸索着遥控器，及时调到了那个频道，听到了：

sentences.en: This building could have killed tens of thousands of people.
sentences.zh: “这座建筑本可能杀死成千上万的人。”

sentences.en: The extraordinary chain of events began with a phone call out of the Bludes
sentences.zh: 这一非凡的事件链始于一个突如其来的电话，

sentences.en: from a student in New Jersey whose professor had told him to write a paper
sentences.zh: 来自新泽西州的一名学生，他的教授让他写一篇论文，

sentences.en: on the Citicorp tower, William LeMessier.
sentences.zh: 关于花旗集团大厦，威廉·勒梅西耶。

sentences.en: And I explained to the student in a telephone call
sentences.zh: “我在电话里向那个学生解释说，

sentences.en: that he could tell his professor.
sentences.zh: 他可以告诉他的教授。”

sentences.en: I was aghaSt. I nearly dropped my baby.
sentences.zh: 我当时惊呆了。我差点把孩子掉在地上。

sentences.en: This was the first time Diane had ever heard of the emergency retrofits,
sentences.zh: 这是黛安第一次听说紧急加固工程、

sentences.en: the round-the-clock weather monitoring, the evacuation plans.
sentences.zh: 全天候的气象监测和疏散计划。

sentences.en: And the involvement of a student.
sentences.zh: 以及一名学生的参与。

sentences.en: So when she heard LeMessier reference a student, a male student.
sentences.zh: 所以当她听到勒梅西耶提到一个学生，一个男学生时。

sentences.en: I, of course, assumed, you know, gosh, there was some guy studying the building as well.
sentences.zh: 我当然以为，天哪，还有个家伙也在研究这座建筑。

sentences.en: And wow, you know, how could I miss this?
sentences.zh: 哇，你知道，我怎么会错过这个呢？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it was pretty remarkable.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是太了不起了。

sentences.en: But I, of course, assumed at the time that there was another fellow
sentences.zh: 但我当时当然以为还有另一个家伙，

sentences.en: who had been a better researcher than I had been.
sentences.zh: 他比我做得更好。

sentences.en: In fact, Diane never even considered that she might be the student in the story.
sentences.zh: 事实上，黛安从未想过她自己可能就是故事里的那个学生。

sentences.en: That is, until she went to a Princeton event honouring her thesis advisor, David Billington.
sentences.zh: 直到她参加了一个普林斯顿大学纪念她论文导师大卫·比林顿（David Billington）的活动。

sentences.en: When I showed up at the event, David said,
sentences.zh: 当我出现在活动现场时，大卫说：

sentences.en: well, have you ever heard of the problems with the Citicorp Centre?
sentences.zh: “好吧，你听说过花旗集团中心的问题吗？”

sentences.en: And I said, yes, isn't that pretty remarkable?
sentences.zh: 我说：“听说过，那不是很了不起吗？”

sentences.en: I wonder who it was that discovered this problem.
sentences.zh: “我真想知道是谁发现了这个问题。”

sentences.en: And he said, you know, Diane, there are very few engineering schools in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 他说：“你知道，黛安，新泽西州没几所工程学院。”

sentences.en: And quite frankly, I know all of them.
sentences.zh: “坦白说，我全都认识。”

sentences.en: And I know the heads of the programs of all of them.
sentences.zh: “我也认识他们所有项目的负责人。”

sentences.en: And I've talked to all of them.
sentences.zh: “而且我都和他们谈过。”

sentences.en: There was no other student from New Jersey that was studying the building except for you.
sentences.zh: “除了你，没有其他新泽西州的学生在研究这座建筑。”

sentences.en: So it must have been you.
sentences.zh: “所以那一定是你。”

sentences.en: Yes, I don't know about any other student.
sentences.zh: “是的，我不知道还有其他学生。”

sentences.en: This is David Billington, the thesis advisor.
sentences.zh: 这是大卫·比林顿，论文导师。

sentences.en: Yes, my name is David Billington.
sentences.zh: “是的，我叫大卫·比林顿。”

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: “没错。”

sentences.en: And I'm an engineer.
sentences.zh: “我是一名工程师。”

sentences.en: Spent 53 years at Princeton as a faculty member.
sentences.zh: “在普林斯顿当了53年的教员。”

sentences.en: I was Diane Hartley's thesis advisor.
sentences.zh: “我是黛安·哈特利的论文导师。”

sentences.en: She wrote the most outstanding thesis of anybody.
sentences.zh: “她写出了所有人中最出色的论文。”

sentences.en: It was a very low.
sentences.zh: “那是一份非常详尽的论文。”

sentences.en: Have you ever seen it?
sentences.zh: “你见过吗？”

sentences.en: Two big volumes.
sentences.zh: “两大卷。”

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: “是的。”

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: “总之。”

sentences.en: To hear Diane Hartley and David Billington tell the story,
sentences.zh: 听黛安·哈特利和大卫·比林顿讲述这个故事，

sentences.en: Diane wasn't some in-your-face know-it-all.
sentences.zh: 黛安并不是那种咄咄逼人的“万事通”。

sentences.en: Here's her version of the events.
sentences.zh: 这是她对事件的描述。

sentences.en: So I was 21 years old and I was a senior at Princeton University where I was studying architecture and urban planning.
sentences.zh: “我当时21岁，是普林斯顿大学的大四学生，主修建筑和城市规划。”

sentences.en: My thesis, I had selected the topic of the Citicorp Centre in New York, which had only recently been completed and occupied.
sentences.zh: “我的论文选题是纽约的花旗集团中心，它当时刚建成并投入使用不久。”

sentences.en: She reached out to LeMessure's firm to get the calculations that they had run.
sentences.zh: 她联系了勒梅西耶的公司，获取了他们运行的计算数据。

sentences.en: And then she tried to replicate the math herself to do the work again from the start and see if she got the same answers as LeMessure's engineers.
sentences.zh: 然后她尝试自己复核数学计算，从头开始做一遍，看看是否能得到与勒梅西耶的工程师们相同的答案。

sentences.en: David Billington, her advisor, asked her to ask LeMessure's firm about the quartering winds.
sentences.zh: 她的导师大卫·比林顿让她向勒梅西耶的公司询问关于斜向风的问题。

sentences.en: The quartering wind, I thought that was a problem and that it should be looked at.
sentences.zh: “斜向风，我觉得那是个问题，应该研究一下。”

sentences.en: So I obtained calculations from the design engineer from LeMessure's office and I concluded the governing loading condition was the wind hitting the corner of the building.
sentences.zh: “所以我从勒梅西耶办公室的设计工程师那里获得了计算结果，我得出的结论是，主要的荷载条件是风吹向建筑的角落。”

sentences.en: But the math just wasn't coming out right.
sentences.zh: 但数学计算结果总是不对。

sentences.en: I was struggling with the calculations.
sentences.zh: 我在计算上遇到了困难。

sentences.en: I assumed, of course, that the engineer had done the right thing and any inconsistency that I might find would be my error.
sentences.zh: 我当然假设工程师做的是对的，我发现的任何不一致之处都是我自己的错误。

sentences.en: You know, the building was standing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大楼还立在那里呢。

sentences.en: After all, she was just a college senior and LeMessure and his people were established, internationally renowned, professional structural engineers.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，她只是一个大学高年级学生，而勒梅西耶和他的团队是久负盛名、享誉国际的专业结构工程师。

sentences.en: Diane got back in touch with LeMessure's firm, although she never talked with LeMessure herself.
sentences.zh: 黛安再次联系了勒梅西耶的公司，尽管她从未与勒梅西耶本人交谈过。

sentences.en: I never called LeMessure.
sentences.zh: “我从未给勒梅西耶打过电话。”

sentences.en: I never said these things that were documented in the various reports that had been published to date.
sentences.zh: “我从未说过迄今为止各种已发表报告中记录的那些话。”

sentences.en: Diane did talk to a junior engineer at LeMessure's New York office named Joel Weinstein.
sentences.zh: 黛安确实与勒梅西耶纽约办公室的一位初级工程师乔尔·温斯坦（Joel Weinstein）谈过。

sentences.en: She showed him her calculations.
sentences.zh: 她向他展示了自己的计算结果。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, no, I didn't feel that I had put my finger on a major problem.
sentences.zh: “但归根结底，不，我不觉得我发现了一个重大问题。”

sentences.en: I assumed I was wrong and wasn't understanding things.
sentences.zh: “我以为是我错了，没理解透彻。”

sentences.en: Even David Bellington, who had told Diane to look into the quartering winds in the first place, didn't think there was any imminent threat.
sentences.zh: 甚至连最初让黛安去研究斜向风的大卫·比林顿，当时也没觉得有什么迫在眉睫的威胁。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think either of us really were in a position to say at the time, you've got to do something, Bill, right away.
sentences.zh: “我的意思是，我不认为我们当时有立场说：‘比尔，你必须马上采取行动。’”

sentences.en: We didn't have that feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们当时没有那种感觉。

sentences.en: I had the feeling that she should talk to the designers and find out whether this quartering wind had been considered, and if so, what was the outcome.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得她应该去和设计师谈谈，弄清楚他们是否考虑过这种侧向风的影响，如果考虑过，结果如何。

sentences.en: But somehow, Diane's discovery got silently passed up the totem pole within LeMessure's firm.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，戴安的发现被勒梅苏尔公司内部悄无声息地层层上报了。

sentences.en: Weinstein must have said, well, I better check with Bill.
sentences.zh: 温斯坦肯定想过，嗯，我最好去和比尔确认一下。

sentences.en: That would have been the logical thing to do, and he probably did that.
sentences.zh: 那本该是合乎逻辑的做法，他很可能也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: I never heard that.
sentences.zh: 我从未听说过这件事。

sentences.en: You never heard it, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想你确实没听说过。

sentences.en: We asked Joel Weinstein, the engineer, about meeting Diane and what happened afterwards, but he says he has no memory of this either way.
sentences.zh: 我们问过工程师乔尔·温斯坦关于他与戴安会面以及之后发生的事情，但他表示对此毫无印象。

sentences.en: Though he does acknowledge that if Diane remembers speaking to him, then it probably happened, and that in such a circumstance, he would have passed her message on to LeMessure.
sentences.zh: 不过他承认，如果戴安记得曾与他交谈过，那很可能确实发生过，在这种情况下，他会把她的信息转达给勒梅苏尔。

sentences.en: So it could be that's why LeMessure remembers speaking to a male student.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能就是为什么勒梅苏尔记得自己是和一个男学生谈过话。

sentences.en: He was complaining Diane Hartley, the student, with Joel Weinstein, his own staffer.
sentences.zh: 他把学生戴安·哈特利和他的员工乔尔·温斯坦搞混了。

sentences.en: Now, of course, it is possible that there was a male student.
sentences.zh: 当然，也可能确实存在过一名男学生。

sentences.en: A third man.
sentences.zh: 第三个人。

sentences.en: Who somehow had the same data as Diane, and actually did talk to LeMessure on the phone.
sentences.zh: 他不知何故掌握了和戴安一样的数据，并且真的在电话里和勒梅苏尔谈过。

sentences.en: But I find it really hard to believe that such a person didn't come forward and claim the spotlight after the story broke.
sentences.zh: 但我实在很难相信，在故事曝光后，这样一个人竟然没有站出来博取关注。

sentences.en: Gender aside, Diane definitely doesn't fit the image of the precocious student.
sentences.zh: 抛开性别不谈，戴安绝对不符合那种早慧学生的形象。

sentences.en: She identified a problem without even recognising the significance of what she had done for decades.
sentences.zh: 她发现了一个问题，甚至在几十年里都没意识到自己所做之事的重大意义。

sentences.en: It's not that I did something.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我做了什么了不起的事。

sentences.en: It's that perhaps my questions helped someone figure something out.
sentences.zh: 而是也许我的提问帮助某人弄清了某些事情。

sentences.en: Perhaps my questions were meant to be.
sentences.zh: 也许我的提问是命中注定的。

sentences.en: I think if I had really realised that there was a problem, and put my finger on it, and raised it up the flagpole,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果我当时真的意识到有问题，并指出了它，还把它上报了，

sentences.en: I could pat myself on the back for having done something that was pretty remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我或许会为自己做了一件相当了不起的事而沾沾自喜。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, I feel like I was a bit player in a play that had a happy ending.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我觉得自己只是一个有着圆满结局的剧目中的小角色。

sentences.en: So yes, she deserves more credit than she's gotten.
sentences.zh: 所以没错，她理应得到比现在更多的赞誉。

sentences.en: You can tell her that, include that, I think, that that's right.
sentences.zh: 你可以告诉她，把这一点也加进去，我想，这才是正确的。

sentences.en: That's, I think, the coda for this.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是这个故事的尾声。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Joel Werner and Sam Greenspan,
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由乔尔·沃纳和萨姆·格林斯潘制作，

sentences.en: with Katie Mingle, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 参与制作的还有凯蒂·明格、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Michael Verdaro, who wrote the AIA Trust white paper about Citicorp Center,
sentences.zh: 特别感谢迈克尔·维达罗，他撰写了关于花旗集团中心的AIA信托白皮书，

sentences.en: Samil Rogavin at the National Academy of Engineering for helping us track down archival audio of William LeMessure,
sentences.zh: 感谢美国国家工程院的萨米尔·罗加文帮助我们找到了威廉·勒梅苏尔的档案音频，

sentences.en: and Alan Bellows of the website Damn Interesting for talking to me about this about two years ago at this point.
sentences.zh: 还要感谢Damn Interesting网站的艾伦·贝洛斯，大约两年前他曾和我谈起过这件事。

sentences.en: We are Project 91.7 Local Public Radio, KALW, in San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山的项目91.7本地公共广播电台，KALW，

sentences.en: and produced out of the offices of ArcSign, a beautiful architecture firm in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 节目是在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的ArcSign办公室制作的。

sentences.en: You can keep up with this show and all the people who make this show on Facebook, Twitter, and Tumblr.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook、Twitter和Tumblr上关注本节目以及所有制作人员。

sentences.en: But if you want to see some pictures of Citicorp Center, go to 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看一些花旗集团中心的照片，请访问99pi.org。

sentences.en: All right, and make sure you say that.
sentences.zh: 好的，一定要把这个说出来。

sentences.en: Wait, sorry, say something again?
sentences.zh: 等等，抱歉，能再说一遍吗？

sentences.en: I say, this is not architecture we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们谈论的不是建筑学。

sentences.en: This is structure, engineering structure.
sentences.zh: 这是结构，工程结构。

sentences.en: I'm very sensitive about that.
sentences.zh: 我对这一点非常敏感。

sentences.en: I don't want to mix up these things.
sentences.zh: 我不想把这些东西混为一谈。

sentences.en: I think that in this case, the Measures design was a brilliant structural design,
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种情况下，勒梅苏尔的设计是一个出色的结构设计，

sentences.en: but it was all covered over, typical of architects, to cover it over so you could never see it.
sentences.zh: 但它被完全遮盖住了，这是建筑师的典型做法，把它遮起来，让你永远看不见它。

sentences.en: Most people make that decision about tall buildings, that they want it to be architecture.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在处理高层建筑时都会做出这种决定，他们希望它是建筑艺术。

sentences.en: And that's why most of them are so bad.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大多数建筑都很糟糕的原因。

sentences.en: But anyway, that is a prejudice.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，这是一种偏见。

sentences.en: So it would be clear this is structure, not architecture.
sentences.zh: 所以要明确一点，这是结构，而不是建筑。

sentences.en: But what we're talking about is structure, not architecture.
sentences.zh: 但我们谈论的是结构，而不是建筑。
